theory.intro: A trigonometric ratio is just a number, so a trigonometric equation is solved like any other equation. When the unknown side sits in the **numerator**, one step finishes the job: multiply both sides by the known side.
facts: $\sin\theta=\dfrac{O}{H}$, $\cos\theta=\dfrac{A}{H}$, $\tan\theta=\dfrac{O}{A}$, where $O$, $A$ and $H$ are measured from the marked angle.
$\sin 30^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{7}$ means exactly the same as $0.5=\dfrac{x}{7}$ — the ratio is a number.
Choose the ratio that uses **the side you are given and the side you want**, ignoring the third side.
When $x$ is in the numerator, multiply both sides by the known denominator: $\sin 38^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{7}$ gives $x=7\sin 38^{\circ}$.
Keep the full calculator value until the last line, then round to the accuracy the question asks for.
steps: Label the sides of the triangle

foundation.question_text: Solve $\sin 41^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{9}$, giving $x$ correct to $2$ decimal places.
Solve $\tan 27^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{14}$, giving $x$ correct to $2$ decimal places.
Solve $\dfrac{x}{6.5}=\cos 58^{\circ}$, giving $x$ correct to $2$ decimal places.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (3.217,0);\coordinate (C) at (3.217,2.700);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,right] {$x$};\draw (C)--(A) node[midway,above left] {$15\text{ cm}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(A)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(B)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$40^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.6cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=B--A--C};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which trigonometric ratio should be used to find $x$? Name the two sides involved.
foundation.solution_text:
The $15$ cm side is the hypotenuse $(H)$.
$x$ is opposite the $40^{\circ}$ angle $(O)$.
The ratio using $O$ and $H$ is $\sin$.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (B) at (0,0);\coordinate (A) at (0,3.465);\coordinate (C) at (2.337,0);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,below] {$x$};\draw (C)--(A) node[midway,above right] {$19\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(A)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(B)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$34^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.6] {angle=B--A--C};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The marked angle is at the top of this triangle. Find $x$ correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
From the $34^{\circ}$ angle, $x$ is the opposite side and $19$ m is the hypotenuse.
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{O}{H}$
$\sin 34^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{19}$
$19\sin 34^{\circ}=x$
$x\approx 10.6\text{ m}$

[tikz]

[/tikz]
This right-angled triangle is drawn on a slant. Find $x$ correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
The right angle is between the two shorter sides, so $7.4$ cm is the hypotenuse and $x$ is opposite the $41^{\circ}$ angle.
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{O}{H}$
$\sin 41^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{7.4}$
$7.4\sin 41^{\circ}=x$
$x\approx 4.9\text{ cm}$
